Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates a well-circumscribed, thin-walled cystic lesion with an air-fluid level in the left lower lobe (retrocardiac region), which is a classic radiographic appearance of an infected intralobar pulmonary sequestration. Other options are inconsistent with the focal, unilateral nature of the finding or the specific morphology (e.g., emphysema is diffuse, TB typically affects upper lobes, and heart failure causes bilateral edema).
